speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned your husband is exhibiting bizarre and agitated behavior; can you describe exactly what he has been saying or doing that concerns you?

speaker: Patient
text: 26-year-old male. The patient has been demonstrating bizarre and agitated behavior for the past 6 weeks. He believes that he is being spied on by the NSA which is also controlling his mind. His wife adds that he has been increasingly withdrawn and intermittently depressed over the last 3 months. He was terminated from his job 4 weeks ago after he ceased attending work. Since his unemployment, he has been focused on creating a device to prevent people from controlling his mind.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Delusional Disorder, Persecutory Type.

The patient's 6-week history of fixed, non-bizarre delusions regarding mind control by the NSA, combined with preserved function in areas other than his work (which he stopped attending due to the delusion), suggests a specific psychotic disorder rather than schizophrenia. Given the onset over 6 weeks and the lack of prominent disorganized speech or negative symptoms other than withdrawal, this fits the criteria for Delusional Disorder.
